message.content:
Below are two ways you can provision a **Google Cloud Compute Engine** instance that has an NVIDIA RTX A6000 GPU and runs **Ubuntu 20.04 LTS**.

---

## 1️⃣  `gcloud` CLI (recommended)

```bash
# 1. Create a project‑specific zone (replace <ZONE> with your preferred zone)
ZONENAME=<ZONE>

# 2. Create a new VM instance
gcloud compute instances create my-rtx-a6000 \
    --zone=$ZONENAME \
    --machine-type=n1-standard-8 \          # 8 vCPU, 30 GB RAM – adjust if needed
    --image-family=ubuntu-2004-lts \
    --image-project=ubuntu-os-cloud \
    --boot-disk-size=100GB \
    --boot-disk-type=pd-balanced \
    --maintenance-policy=MIGRATE \
    --scopes=https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform \
    --tags=http-server,https-server \
    --metadata-from-file startup-script=startup.sh \   # optional: script to install drivers
    --accelerator=type=nvidia-tesla-a6000,count=1 \
    --reservation-affinity=any
```

### What each flag does

| Flag | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `--machine-type` | CPU/RAM configuration. `n1-standard-8` gives 8 vCPUs & 30 GB RAM. |
| `--image-family` / `--image-project` | Pulls the latest Ubuntu 20.04 LTS image from the official Ubuntu Cloud image repository. |
| `--boot-disk-size` / `--boot-disk-type` | Sets the size & performance tier of the boot disk. |
| `--accelerator` | Adds one NVIDIA RTX A6000 GPU (`nvidia-tesla-a6000`). |
| `--reservation-affinity` | Allows the instance to use any available GPU reservation. |

> **Tip:** If you plan to run GPU workloads, consider installing the NVIDIA driver via a startup script:

```bash
#!/bin/bash
sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get install -y nvidia-driver-535
```

Save that script as `startup.sh` and reference it with `--metadata-from-file`.

---

## 2️⃣  REST API (JSON payload)

If you prefer to use the Compute Engine REST API directly (e.g., from a custom application), here’s a minimal JSON body you can POST to `https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/{PROJECT_ID}/zones/{ZONE}/instances`.

```json
{
  "name": "my-rtx-a6000",
  "machineType": "projects/{PROJECT_ID}/zones/{ZONE}/machineTypes/n1-standard-8",
  "disks": [
    {
      "boot": true,
      "autoDelete": true,
      "initializeParams": {
        "sourceImage": "projects/ubuntu-os-cloud/global/images/family/ubuntu-2004-lts",
        "diskSizeGb": 100,
        "diskType": "projects/{PROJECT_ID}/zones/{ZONE}/diskTypes/pd-balanced"
      }
    }
  ],
  "networkInterfaces": [
    {
      "network": "global/networks/default",
      "accessConfigs": [
        { "type": "ONE_TO_ONE_NAT", "name": "External NAT" }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "serviceAccounts": [
    {
      "email": "default",
      "scopes": ["https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform"]
    }
  ],
  "guestAccelerators": [
    {
      "acceleratorCount": 1,
      "acceleratorType": "projects/{PROJECT_ID}/zones/{ZONE}/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-tesla-a6000"
    }
  ],
  "metadata": {
    "items": [
      {
        "key": "startup-script",
        "value": "#!/bin/bash\napt-get update\napt-get install -y nvidia-driver-535"
      }
    ]
  },
  "tags": {
    "items": ["http-server", "https-server"]
  }
}
```

Replace `{PROJECT_ID}` and `{ZONE}` with your actual project ID and zone.  
Send this payload with an authenticated POST request to the Compute Engine API endpoint.

---

### Quick checklist

- ✅ Verify that the **GPU quota** for your project includes at least one RTX A6000.  
- ✅ Ensure the **billing account** is attached to the project.  
- ✅ After creation, SSH into the instance and run `nvidia-smi` to confirm the driver installation.

Let me know if you’d like help automating this via Terraform, Deployment Manager, or another IaC tool!
